subject: Post-demo: Performance / SLO recap & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>
Cc: Sonia Patel <sonia.patel@fintechco.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Performance / SLO recap & next steps

Alex & Sonia — thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we can align on MAP items for the POC.

High-level SLOs you shared (confirm/correct):
- Latency: P95 generation latency <= 300ms (interactive routing) for 75–200 token responses; burst tolerance to 450ms.
- Throughput: sustained 60 requests/sec for peak hour traffic; 240k tokens/min as a ballpark.
- Concurrency: support 200 concurrent sessions with streaming enabled.
- Streaming: token-by-token streaming required for progressive UI; client expects SSE/WebSocket-compatible chunking.
- Availability: 99.9% monthly for inference endpoints.

Questions we have to scope the POC and confirm MAP:
1) Typical and max sequence lengths (including system + user + expected assistant tokens).
2) % of requests that require streaming vs. full response at once.
3) Any large-attachment or multimodal payloads that would change throughput assumptions.
4) Target region(s) for latency goals (you mentioned west-coast users primarily).

Requested artifacts from FintechCo for next week (if possible):
- Representative prompt set (sample_prompts.txt) and expected token lengths.
- Peak/hour load profile (per-minute QPS) — helps shape batching/async config.
- Any compliance/network constraints for Private deployment testing.

Next steps / owners: 
- Marissa: coordinate POC run and initial load test (target week of June 21). (attachment: FTCO_SLO_checklist_v1.xlsx)
- Marcus: publish baseline microbench numbers for the recommended model variant and streaming config.
- Alex: share sample_prompts.txt + expected seq length by Mon (6/21).

If that looks right, Sonia/Alex can reply with the artifacts and we’ll schedule a 60-min performance workshop to lock in the MAP and test plan.

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0199

Attachment: FTCO_SLO_checklist_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)
Attachment: sample_prompts.txt (text)

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sonia Patel <sonia.patel@fintechco.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Performance / SLO recap & next steps

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming most of this is accurate. A few clarifications: 
- P95 target: we want <= 300ms for the primary flow (account lookup + response generation). For fallback/background tasks, 1s is fine.
- Throughput: 60 req/s sustained, yes; bursts up to 150 req/s for short windows (~2–3 min).
- Concurrency: 200 active concurrent streaming sessions is correct.
- Streaming: SSE preferred. We use an internal gateway that handles SSE to mobile/web clients.

We’re attaching sample_prompts.txt and a short load profile (inline — see below). Typical sequence length is 120 tokens average, 450 tokens max including system and history. ~70% of requests use streaming.

Inline load profile: peak hour: sustained 60 QPS; occasional spikes to 150 QPS for 2–3 minute bursts; evening peak concentrated in US-PST region.

We’ll also add the network diagram and any compliance notes to the shared Drive link. Please schedule the performance workshop — we’re available Tue/Wed next week.

— Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Product, FintechCo
alex.johnson@fintechco.com

Attachment: sample_prompts.txt (provided)
Attachment: network_arch_diagram.png (provided)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 11:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Performance / SLO recap & next steps

Thanks — pulling in a few baseline numbers to set expectations. Quick notes: 
- Recommended config: rwd-gpt-7B-q4 + streaming enabled with small chunk size (8–16 tokens) for lowest latency.
- Local microbench (west-coast instance, p4d-equivalent): P50 60ms, P95 ~220–280ms for 75–150 token outputs with streaming; these include model execution + kernel overhead but exclude network egress to client.
- With batching tuned for 60 QPS (avg seq 120 tokens) we estimate sustained cost and that Dedicated 4-GPU pool will handle 60 QPS with headroom for 2–3x short bursts before autoscale kicks in.

Open items for POC:
- Precise token distribution across requests (samples ideally).
- Confirm whether you need per-user KV caching (helps for repeated contexts).
- Any special network/DDoS protections on your gateway we should be aware of.

I’ll drop the microbench CSV into the shared Drive link and include an initial load-test run URL once the POC infra is provisioned.

Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

Attachment: microbench_results_westcoast.csv (referenced in Drive)

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Performance / SLO recap & next steps

Alex — looping in the infra plan for the POC and a proposed workshop agenda.

Proposed POC plan (high level):
1) Day 0: exchange sample_prompts + enable test API keys (sandbox).
2) Day 1–2: baseline microbench + small-scale streaming test (validate chunking behavior).
3) Day 3: scaled load runs up to 60 QPS sustained and 150 QPS short bursts; monitor P95/P99 and token throughput.
4) Day 4: tuning (batching, concurrency, KV cache) and re-run.
5) Day 5: POC summary + decision criteria report (we’ll fill FTCO_SLO_checklist_v1.xlsx).

Workshop agenda (60m):
- 10m: goals & success criteria (you confirm P95/throughput/concurrency).
- 20m: review sample prompts & typical request flows.
- 20m: live baseline microbench + expected differences for Private vs Hosted.
- 10m: next steps / MAP assignment.

Can we lock Wed 23 Jun 2027 10:00–11:00 PT for the workshop? If that works I’ll send a calendar invite and pre-provision sandbox keys. Also please share any IP allowlists for our sandbox to reach your gateway.

Thanks — Dev
Dev Patel
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.com

Attachment: network_runbook.md (referenced)

Subject: Re: Post-demo: Performance / SLO recap & next steps

Thanks everyone — Wed 23 Jun 10:00 PT works for us. We’ve uploaded the sample_prompts.txt and network_arch_diagram.png to the shared folder and added an allowlist for Redwood sandbox IPs.

Action items (confirmed):
- FintechCo (Alex/Sonia): share any compliance/network constraints and full prompt set by EOD Tue (21 Jun) — done.
- Redwood (Marissa/Marcus/Dev): provision sandbox keys, run baseline, and present microbench during workshop.
- All: complete FTCO_SLO_checklist_v1.xlsx during the POC and agree on decision criteria at the end.

Looking forward — Sonia
